The Louisiana Purchase was a significant land acquisition made by the United States from France in 1803. The key figures involved in the negotiation and signing of the treaty were Robert Livingston and James Monroe, who were American diplomats, and Francois Barbe-Marbois, the French negotiator. Thomas Jefferson was the President of the United States at the time and authorized the purchase, but he did not personally sign the treaty. The actual signing was done by the diplomats involved in the negotiations.
